An exceptional independent school in Wokingham, Berkshire where children flourish with confidence, curiosity and character.
Holme Grange School in Wokingham, Berkshire provides a rich and inspiring education for children aged 9 months to 16 years, combining individualised teaching, outstanding co-curricular opportunities and one continuous school journey.
Why Families Choose Holme Grange
You want your child to feel happy, confident and inspired to learn. At Holme Grange, every part of school life is designed to help your child flourish academically, socially and personally. Whether exploring the school farm, performing on stage or discovering new passions in the classroom and beyond, your child is encouraged to grow in confidence, develop independence and build a lifelong love of learning within one connected and supportive school community.
Outstanding Pastoral Care
Every child deserves to feel known, supported and understood. At Holme Grange, exceptional pastoral care and strong relationships help your child grow in confidence, resilience and self-belief.
Responsive and individualised teaching enables your child to make exceptional progress with confidence. Ranked Top 5 nationally in The Sunday Times Parent Power 2026 (Best Independent School 11-16)
Rich Co-Curricular Opportunities
One day your child is exploring the school farm. The next they are performing on stage, competing on the sports field or discovering a new passion beyond the classroom.
One Continuous School Journey
From first discoveries in Nursery to growing independence in Senior School, your child benefits from continuity, familiarity and long-term support within one connected school community.
GROW WITH US From Nursery to Senior School, every stage of the Holme Grange journey is designed to help your child flourish in confidence, curiosity and character.
Nursery 9 months – 4+ years

Your child’s first school experiences should feel secure, inspiring and full of discovery. At Little Grange Nursery, confidence, independence and curiosity grow through exploration, creativity and play.
Your child builds strong foundations, develops confidence and discovers a love of learning within a stimulating and supportive environment.
Challenge, creativity and opportunity encourage your child to think independently, grow in resilience and make exceptional progress both inside and beyond the classroom.
Your child develops independence, self-belief and the confidence to thrive within a supportive and ambitious learning environment.

pageCache.pageTitle: GCSE Results - Holme Grange School, Wokingham, Berkshire
pageCache.text:
GCSE Results
GCSE Results
We are delighted to celebrate another year of outstanding GCSE results, reflecting the hard work of our pupils, the dedication of our staff and the support of our families.
A Year of Outstanding Achievement
Our pupils achieved exceptional outcomes across a broad range of subjects, placing Holme Grange among the highest-performing independent schools nationally. As a non-selective co-educational school, we are proud that pupils of all abilities are supported and challenged to achieve their personal best.
Headline Achievements
With an impressive set of results this year, our pupils achieved:
These outcomes are a testament to the commitment, resilience and ambition of our pupils.
Core subjects once again demonstrated exceptional performance, with 98% of pupils achieving 9 – 4 in Mathematics, 99% in English Language and 95% in English Literature, with high proportions at the top grades. Science was particularly impressive, with 100% pass rates across Biology, Chemistry and Physics and more than 90% of candidates achieving grades 9 – 7. This continues a proud tradition at Holme Grange of consecutive years with 100% Science pass rates. Notably, 56% of pupils achieved grade 9 in both Chemistry and Physics – the school’s highest ever results in these subjects.
Modern Foreign Languages also excelled, with every candidate in French achieving grades 9 – 7, including 63% at grade 9, while German secured a 100% pass rate with 80% at 9 – 7. Humanities and Arts subjects also shone, with 65% of grades at 9 – 7 in History, 56% in Geography, 53% in Religious Studies, 62% in Food Preparation and Nutrition, and 83% in Design Technology. Art and Drama both achieved a 100% pass rate. Business Studies and Computer Science also achieved strong results, with Business securing 47% at grades 9 – 7 and Computer Science achieving 58% at grades 9 – 7.
Excellence extended beyond GCSEs, with BTEC pathways also delivering outstanding success. Music BTEC pupils achieved 86% at Distinction*, Animal Care celebrated excellent outcomes with 67% of pupils awarded Distinction* or Distinction, and Sport was equally impressive, with GCSE PE securing a 100% pass rate and BTEC Sport achieving a 100% pass rate including 33% at Distinction.
Reflecting on this final set of results before handing over the leadership of the school, Claire Robinson shared her pride:“I could not be prouder of our pupils and staff. Behind every grade lies a story of courage, resilience and self-belief. While we rightly celebrate these superb outcomes I remind our young people that grades do not define them, their character will ultimately shape their futures. To see them excel, thrive and embody our ethos of going above and beyond is the greatest legacy I could ask for as I hand over the leadership of this wonderful school.”
Our new Headteacher, Pippa Adams, also shared her excitement for the future:“These results are a testament to the strong foundations laid at Holme Grange. I am excited to build on this success and ensure that every pupil continues to be nurtured, challenged and inspired. Our community can be proud not only of the grades achieved but of the values and character that shine through in our pupils.”
At Holme Grange, we are proud to be a non-selective, award-winning independent through school where pupils are nurtured, challenged and inspired to be brave, bold and to believe in themselves. The Class of 2025 have made us proud, and we look forward to seeing all they will go on to achieve.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from Headteacher, Mrs Pippa Adams
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to Holme Grange School
At Holme Grange, we believe education is a lifelong journey shaped by meaning, purpose, connection and wisdom. From 9 months through to 16, children are supported and inspired to grow as confident individuals who are curious about the world and compassionate towards others.
Within our ambitious and nurturing environment, pupils are encouraged to understand themselves, build strong relationships and engage thoughtfully with the world around them. Kindness, respect, integrity, responsibility and compassion sit at the heart of daily life at Holme Grange. As a through school, older pupils become positive role models for younger children, helping to create a strong sense of community and belonging across every stage of the school.
As a co-educational school, we believe boys and girls benefit enormously from learning, growing and working alongside one another. Sharing experiences and perspectives helps pupils develop mutual respect, confidence and understanding, while building the positive relationships and social skills that prepare them for life beyond school.
Learning at Holme Grange is rich in opportunity and discovery. Whether exploring the natural world, developing creative talents or preparing for the opportunities and challenges of an increasingly digital future, children are encouraged to think independently, ask questions and approach learning with curiosity and confidence.
Academic excellence is balanced with outstanding pastoral care, ensuring every pupil feels supported, valued and inspired to achieve their very best. Beyond the classroom, a rich co-curricular programme allows children to discover new interests, develop resilience and build confidence through a wide range of experiences. A strong culture of philanthropy also runs throughout the school, encouraging pupils to contribute positively to both local and global communities.
We understand the pace of modern family life and offer flexible wraparound care to support families throughout the school week. From Breakfast Club and Extended Day to Prep Club and a wide range of extra-curricular activities, children benefit from a safe, engaging and nurturing environment until 5:45pm Monday to Thursday and 5:30pm on Fridays. A regularly reviewed minibus network also supports families across the local area.
Above all, our aim is to prepare young people not only for future success, but for lives filled with purpose, kindness and positive contribution.
I warmly invite you to visit Holme Grange and experience the spirit, ambition and warmth of our community for yourself.

Scholarships and Bursaries
Scholarships
At Holme Grange, scholarships recognise pupils who demonstrate exceptional talent, potential and commitment in their chosen field.
Our Scholarship Programme is about more than recognising achievement. Scholars are encouraged to develop their talents further, embrace new opportunities and make a positive contribution to school life, while inspiring others through their enthusiasm and commitment.
Scholarships are available in Academic, Art, Drama, Music and Sport for entry into Years 7 and 9.
Scholarship Entry Points
Scholarships are available at two entry points into our Senior School:
Year 7 (11+)
Scholarships for entry into Year 7 are awarded during the Autumn Term of Year 6, ready for pupils to begin their scholarship journey the following September.
Year 9 (13+)
Scholarships for entry into Year 9 are awarded during the Autumn Term of Year 8, ready for pupils to join Year 9 the following September.
Explore Our Scholarships
Every scholarship recognises a different area of talent, but all Holme Grange Scholars share a commitment to making the most of their abilities and contributing positively to the wider life of the School.
Explore each scholarship below to find out more about what we look for, the opportunities available to scholars and the application and assessment process.
Academic
An academic scholar will be expected to contribute to the intellectual and academic life of the school by being fully engaged in opportunities and activities. We expect scholars to perform at the highest academic levels in their subjects and to be role models for others. They should exhibit the core values of self-discipline and a love for learning, focusing on broadening their knowledge and skills essential for success in academia. Their leadership skills are nurtured as we equip them to meet the challenges of the 21st-century learner. Academic Scholars will be supported and guided by the Head of Academic Scholars and are expected to work with a high degree of independence. They will meet regularly to discuss opportunities, collaborate on projects, and plan for events and competitions. The Head of Academic Scholars will organise enrichment events and trips throughout the year.
On the Admissions Morning, applicants sit a one-hour computer based assessment in Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning and Mathematics. They will complete an English reading and writing task and attend an interview with the Headteacher and Head of Senior School, where they are asked to bring an object of interest and a piece of work they are particularly proud of.
THE ACADEMIC SCHOLARS’ EXPERIENCE: EXCLUSIVE OPPORTUNITIES AND BENEFITS
Gain a national award (CREST Award)
Attend academic scholar trips and excursions
Attend external conferences and seminars
Visit universities
Engage in STEAM workshops
Hear inspirational visiting speakers
Lead Scholars’ assemblies
Participate in collaborative events and activities
Art
To be considered for an Art Scholarship, applicants must:
Art Scholars are likely to have a growing portfolio of work.
Applicants must bring a portfolio including a minimum of three pieces completed independently over the last 18 months. One piece should be inspired by an artist’s creation.
Applicants will sit a 45-minute practical and complete a 15-minute imaginative task, for which no preparation is necessary.
They will also be expected to discuss their work and passion for art with the Head of Art and Design.
Applicants will attend an interview with the Headteacher and Head of Senior School, where they are asked to bring their portfolio.
THE ART SCHOLARS’ EXPERIENCE: EXCLUSIVE OPPORTUNITIES AND BENEFITS
Engage with numerous art and design opportunities
Attend fortnightly meetings
Attend exclusive, specialised workshops
Drama
To be considered for a Drama Scholarship applicants must:
Drama Scholars are likely to have a portfolio of productions and speech and drama exams.
Applicants must be prepared to perform, from memory, two contrasting monologues. Each piece must last no longer than two minutes.
Applicants will be interviewed by the Heads of Drama for Senior School and Prep School about their involvement in Drama and Performing Arts, both in and out of school. The interview will include questions on their interest in theatre in general and any productions the candidate may have seen.
Applicants should bring a portfolio of work they have been involved in. This can include LAMDA/Trinity College certificates (or similar), as well as details of productions they have seen. If they attend any drama clubs or lessons outside school, they may wish to bring a reference from their teacher; however, this is not compulsory.
Applicants will also attend an interview with the Headteacher and Head of Senior School, where they are asked to bring their portfolio.
THE DRAMA SCHOLARS’ EXPERIENCE: EXCLUSIVE OPPORTUNITIES AND BENEFITS
Demonstrate a passion for Drama and Theatre
Engage with numerous performance opportunities
Attend bi-weekly meetings
Attend specialised workshops and theatre trips
Music
To be considered for a Music Scholarship, applicants must:
Music Scholars are likely to have a portfolio of performances and may show an interest in composition.
Applicants are invited to audition are required to perform two contrasting pieces if presenting one instrument. If presenting two instruments, they must perform a piece on each. They are also encouraged to sing a short piece, unless voice is already one of their instruments.
The audition, conducted by the Director of Music and Head of Prep Music, will include a sight-reading and aural test appropriate to their grade. Applicants will also be asked to perform one or two scales.
Applicants will attend an interview with the Headteacher and Head of Senior School, where they are asked to bring their portfolio.
THE MUSIC SCHOLARS’ EXPERIENCE: EXCLUSIVE OPPORTUNITIES AND BENEFITS
Demonstrate a passion for music
Have performed in a range of concerts
Demonstrate their commitment to regular practice
Be an ambassador for the subject
Attend extensive performance opportunities
Spearhead or lead musical initiatives
Perform in soloist concerts and school events
Participate in informal lunchtime music concerts
Sport
To be considered for a Sports Scholarship applicants must:
Sport scholars are likely to have a portfolio of achievement.
Applicants will be invited to the school for assessment and observation.
They will be interviewed by the Directors of Boys’ or Girls’ Sport.
The assessment will include tests of stamina, speed, flexibility, agility, strength, and coordination.
Applicants will also attend an interview with the Headteacher and Head of Senior School, where they are asked to bring their portfolio of achievements.
Applicants will be assessed in our core sports: • Girls: hockey, netball, football, cricket • Boys: football, rugby, hockey, cricket
We also welcome applications from those who demonstrate exceptional ability in specialist sports, for example gymnastics, swimming, or athletics.
THE SPORT SCHOLARS’ EXPERIENCE: EXCLUSIVE OPPORTUNITIES AND BENEFITS
Demonstrate a passion for sport.
Represent a club
Demonstrate their commitment to regular training
Undertake sports leadership training and opportunities
Attend half termly meetings

Financial Assistance
Bursaries
Scholarships recognise exceptional talent and potential. Separately, Holme Grange offers means-tested bursaries to support families who may not otherwise be able to consider a Holme Grange education.
Bursaries are based on a family’s financial circumstances rather than a child’s particular talent or ability. Pupils are still required to complete the School’s usual admissions assessment to ensure that Holme Grange is the right educational environment for them.
Families may apply for a bursary during the academic year preceding their preferred year of entry. Applications cannot be considered more than one academic year in advance.
As part of the application process, the School will consider the financial circumstances of both parents and any current partners, where applicable. This includes income, capital, benefits and other relevant financial information. Supporting documentation will be required and applications may be reviewed by independent auditors.
All bursary applications are treated in strict confidence and any award made is subject to annual review.
For September 2027 entry, bursaries are available to Senior School applicants only. The application deadline will be confirmed shortly.
Contact Admissions
Choosing whether to apply for a scholarship can raise questions, and our Admissions team will be happy to talk you through the opportunities available and the application process.

Holme Grange is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment.

Care & Wellbeing
At Holme Grange School, pastoral care sits at the heart of everything we do. We are committed to fostering a supportive, inclusive and nurturing environment where every pupil is known, supported and valued. Our strong pastoral culture ensures that pupils thrive not only academically, but also socially and emotionally, developing the confidence, resilience and wellbeing they need to flourish.
A Holistic Approach to Pastoral Care
Pastoral care at Holme Grange is not an add-on – it is embedded into everyday school life. Through dedicated pastoral teams, mentoring programmes and strong communication between staff, pupils and parents, we provide a joined-up approach that prioritises emotional and mental wellbeing alongside academic excellence.
“Pastoral care is not merely a concept; it is an action. At Holme Grange, it is something we live out through what we do.”
Quality First Form Tutoring
Every pupil benefits from high-quality, consistent and proactive pastoral support through our form tutor system. Form tutors are the first point of contact for pupils and families, building strong relationships and ensuring that each child feels listened to, understood and supported throughout their school journey.
Dedicated Heads of Year
Our Heads of Year team play a key role in overseeing both the pastoral and academic progress of pupils within their year group. They work closely with form tutors, parents and senior leaders to:
Monitor pupil wellbeing and progress
Promote positive behaviour and high expectations
Ensure a calm, structured and supportive environment
Wellbeing Support in Action
Pastoral care at Holme Grange is visible, practical and purposeful. Our wellbeing provision includes:
ELSA support in Prep and Senior School
Counselling provision where additional support is needed
A Safe and Inclusive School Community
We are proud of our inclusive school culture, underpinned by clear expectations, kindness and mutual respect. Our pastoral framework includes:
Working in Partnership with Parents
We believe that the best pastoral care is achieved through strong home–school partnerships. Regular communication, parent workshops, forums and ongoing dialogue ensure that pupils benefit from a consistent and supportive approach both at school and at home.
Diversity and inclusion awareness
Student leadership and mentoring opportunities
Why Pastoral Care Matters
The impact of strong pastoral care is seen in pupil confidence, wellbeing and success. By prioritising emotional and social development, Holme Grange equips pupils with the skills to navigate challenges, build positive relationships and achieve their full potential.
Pastoral care at Holme Grange School is a fundamental pillar of our commitment to developing well-rounded, compassionate and resilient young people, prepared for life beyond the classroom.

pageCache.text:
Senior School
The Senior part of our School was opened in 2015. We’ve seen our pupil numbers in Year 11 grow from just 2 in 2015 to over 370 in 2025. At Holme Grange we have a proven history of teaching our senior pupils with excellent results. Our commitment to personalised learning provides them with an invaluable advantage as they move onto the next stages of their educational journey. Supported, guided and challenged by dedicated and passionate staff, Senior School pupils can personalise their academic programme through the broad range of subjects available in the run up to their GCSEs.
During Years 7 – 11 pupil welfare is at the heart of everything we do. In Senior School pupils develop into adolescence in a familiar and nurturing environment. This results in confident individuals who are strong independent learners and are ready to take on life’s challenges.
As the most senior pupils in the School, they have ample opportunity to develop their leadership potential by taking on leadership roles. They can earn positions such as Head of School and Head of House and will represent Holme Grange at events. In Year 11 pupils are encouraged to become Peer Mentors for those in Year 7. Peer mentors will be trained in listening skills and are there to support anyone who might be struggling. These roles can help develop a sense of self-worth and moral responsibilities.
"My daughter graduated with an impressive set of GCSE results enabling her to reach her potential and securing a place of her choice for further education."

pageCache.pageTitle: History of Holme Grange Independent School, Wokingham, Berkshire, UK
pageCache.text:
The History of Holme Grange
Holme Grange was founded in 1945 when forty boys were transferred from Eaton House School in London. Over the years, the school has progressed, expanded and developed into the vibrant, innovative and forward-thinking institution it is today. However, one element has remained constant: its valued ethos of a family feel with traditional values.
We firmly believe in offering a broad, varied and balanced curriculum, creating numerous opportunities for all children to discover their unique talents. Providing these opportunities lies at the heart of what we do, and our facilities reflect this commitment. While the school originated in a beautiful Grade II Listed Building, built in 1883 by Norman Shaw, and continues to operate from this historic site, it has seen many additions and enhancements, as illustrated in our timeline.
Our approach to the site reflects our vision for the school. Holme Grange is a busy, buzzing and stimulating environment – a fantastic place to learn and work. It is undoubtedly forward-thinking and dynamic, yet it steadfastly upholds traditional values and high expectations. We challenge pupils to make the most of their talents and strive for excellence. Similarly, we challenge our twenty-two-acre site to provide the best possible opportunities for every phase of the school, ensuring we continue to deliver exceptional education in the Wokingham area.

Little Grange Nusery
Little Grange Nursery provides a bespoke experience, fostering strong parent partnerships and supporting your child throughout their nursery journey. Our focus on quality education, fun, and outdoor learning helps children leave with confidence, curiosity, and a passion for life and learning.
We pride ourselves on offering the best early years provision, laying the foundation for your child’s educational journey. Our holistic approach emphasises the development of our youngest children through quality outdoor learning, sustainability, and a child-centred philosophy. This fosters a love of nature and inspires a lifelong enthusiasm for learning.
Our flexible provision requires a minimum attendance of 2 full days. We offer both all-year-round and term-time-only options. The nursery is open from 7:30am to 6pm, 50 weeks a year.
The Little Gems
At Little Grange Nursery, our little gems are the extra touches we offer – provisions and enriching experiences that help children shine and go beyond the everyday.
Ballet A weekly session led by a Melody Bear Dance coach, introducing children to dance through imaginative movement, rhythm and storytelling.
Sport Each week, children take part in a P.E. session led by a specialist teacher from Holme Grange School, supporting physical development, coordination and confidence through active play.
Music A weekly music lesson delivered by a specialist teacher from Holme Grange School, introducing children to rhythm, instruments and the joy of making music together.
Science Lab Our dedicated EYFS Science Room sparks curiosity and builds early science skills through hands-on opportunities to observe, investigate and evaluate the world around them.
The Den Our sensory room provides a calming, nurturing space that supports early emotional well-being, helping children feel safe, settled and ready to learn.
Yoga A weekly session run by PlayTime Yoga, supporting children’s wellbeing, balance and mindfulness through playful movement and relaxation.
Little Muddy Boots A unique weekly garden and nature club led by external specialists, offering hands-on outdoor learning and exploration.
Little Grange – where curiosity begins and confidence grows, making our Nursery the premier choice for families.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pre-Prep at Holme Grange | Independent Primary Education (Ages 5–7)
pageCache.text:
Pre-Prep
When children join Holme Grange in the Pre-Prep School, they become part of a family-orientated community where good manners, care for others and kindness are highly valued. We aim to provide our pupils with opportunities to imagine, question and enjoy all that Holme Grange has to offer.
Teaching is both rigorous and fun – the two go hand in hand. We believe children thrive when challenged and stretched, not only through high expectations but also by encouraging them to ask “What if?” and “Why?”
Reception children spend most of their day in “The Hive,” a purpose-built space designed to provide a quieter, more relaxed environment. This allows them to be part of the larger school community while enjoying a setting tailored to their needs. Pupils in Year 1 and Year 2 have the majority of their lessons in classrooms located within the main school building.
For more information about entry into Pre-Prep, click here.
The Pre-Prep teaching team clearly have a passion for what they do. Their level of expertise and experience shows in the way the draw out the very best from the children.
